A is rebreathing, B is a breath hold, C is the recovery after hyperventilation
questions.why: A pause that follows a burst of deep rapid breathing is the post hyperventilation apnea, produced by a PCO2 driven below the threshold that normally keeps the centers firing. A steady climb in both rate and depth over minutes is rebreathing, because bag CO2 keeps rising. A flat stretch followed by one large breath is a voluntary breath hold ending at the breakpoint. The other combinations misread the key feature, which is whether the pause was forced by a low CO2 or chosen by the subject.
questions.answerText: A is the recovery after hyperventilation, B is rebreathing, C is a breath hold

questions.q: A swimmer hyperventilates hard, then swims underwater and loses consciousness without ever feeling a strong urge to breathe. Trace the sequence that explains this.
options: Hyperventilation loaded the blood with so much extra oxygen that it masked the urge to breathe
Low starting PCO2 delayed the urge to breathe while exercise consumed oxygen, so PO2 fell too far
High starting PCO2 blunted the central chemoreceptors, so no signal to breathe was ever generated
Swimming stimulated lung stretch receptors that actively suppressed the urge to breathe
questions.why: The maneuver lowers PCO2 without meaningfully raising oxygen stores, so the CO2 alarm is postponed while swimming burns oxygen fast, and PO2 can reach the level that causes blackout before the breakpoint ever arrives. Hemoglobin is already about 98 percent saturated on room air, so hyperventilation cannot load much extra oxygen. Hyperventilation lowers PCO2 rather than raising it, so the high PCO2 explanation has the direction backward. Stretch receptors shorten inspiration and do not suppress the chemical drive.
questions.answerText: Low starting PCO2 delayed the urge to breathe while exercise consumed oxygen, so PO2 fell too far

questions.q: A subject rebreathes from a bag fitted with a CO2 absorber, so bag CO2 stays near zero while oxygen falls. Predict the ventilation trace.
options: Ventilation stays flat throughout, because only CO2 is able to drive breathing
Ventilation rises steadily from the very first breath, just as in ordinary rebreathing
Ventilation changes little at first, then rises sharply once PO2 falls below 60 mmHg
Ventilation falls progressively as oxygen is steadily removed from the bag
questions.why: Removing the CO2 removes the main drive, so the early part of the trial is nearly silent, and the increase waits until arterial PO2 drops onto the steep part of the peripheral chemoreceptor response near 60 mmHg. A steady rise from the first breath is what happens without the absorber, when CO2 is free to accumulate. Ventilation does not fall, because hypoxia excites rather than inhibits the carotid bodies at these levels. It does not stay flat forever either, since the hypoxic drive eventually takes over.
questions.answerText: Ventilation changes little at first, then rises sharply once PO2 falls below 60 mmHg

questions.q: In a rebreathing trial, ventilation begins climbing when bag CO2 reaches about 45 mmHg, at a moment when bag PO2 is still 105 mmHg. What does this timing show?
options: Oxygen drives the response, since both gases were changing at once
Neither gas drives the response, since the change is caused by bag rebreathing itself
CO2 drives the response, since ventilation rose while oxygen was still normal
Both gases drive the response equally, since each moved from its starting value
questions.why: A PO2 of 105 mmHg is normal and leaves the peripheral chemoreceptors nearly silent, so the only stimulus that has changed enough to matter at that moment is the CO2, which is why ventilation tracks it. Attributing the rise to oxygen ignores that oxygen has not yet fallen anywhere near the 60 mmHg threshold. The act of rebreathing changes the gases but is not itself a stimulus. Calling the two equal ignores the very different sensitivities, which is exactly what this trial is designed to reveal.
questions.answerText: CO2 drives the response, since ventilation rose while oxygen was still normal
